einzeiler: Sarah Hepola explores the untold stories of the original Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
kurzfassung: Sarah Hepola explores the history and impact of the original Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad. The podcast highlights the personal experiences of the women behind the global pop culture phenomenon. Listeners will hear about the triumphs, controversies, and complexities of the squad over eight episodes.
stichpunkte: Sarah Hepola investigates the history of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders starting in 1972.
The podcast features the original voices of the cheerleaders for the first time.
The squad introduced a new dynamic to professional football and television.
The iconic uniform originated from creative imagination.
Cheerleaders faced complex expectations regarding beauty, intelligence, and behavior.
Members navigated major lawsuits and cultural shifts, including Playboy appearances.
The series addresses the lack of proper compensation and heavy demands on the women.
The eight-episode podcast explores high kicks, scandals, and controversies.

clips.text: A former cheerleader expresses that nothing else in her life could ever match the experience of being on the squad.

beschreibung: The original Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders squad burst onto the field back in 1972—the same year Title IX passed, the same year Deep Throat came out, and a year before Roe v. Wade. Sarah Hepola digs into the untold stories behind the global pop culture phenomenon, from the stripper who allegedly inspired the squad’s creation, to a scandalous Playboy cover shoot that was partly a battle over fair wages, to the ongoing debate about sexuality and women’s bodies in a post-#MeToo world. The result is a vibrant mix of history, cultural criticism, and storytelling, featuring interviews with New Yorker writer Jia Tolentino, award-winning novelist Ben Fountain, Oscar-nominated director Dana Adam Shapiro, local television sports legend Dale Hansen, folk-writing hero Joe Nick Patoski, and a whole bunch of cheerleaders whose names you don’t know yet—but should.
